title: Customer Data Access Certification and Review Playbook
summary: Practical playbook for certifying access to customer data under the RBAC v2 migration. Covers policy design constraints, automated evidence extraction, SIEM export contract, reviewer flows, and step-by-step remediation guidance to reach quarterly certification SLAs.
background: As part of RBAC v2 rollout we need an operationalized certification process focused on customer-data access paths (S3/Buckets, DB tables, product APIs, export endpoints). Current ad-hoc reviews lack consistent evidence and are costly to audit. This doc prescribes a repeatable cadence and the automation surface required to produce forensic-grade evidence for internal reviewers and external auditors.
objectives: Define a minimal, auditable certification rubric for all roles that can access customer PII or exported artifacts.
Automate evidence collection so each certification candidate includes policy, last-use telemetry, bounding conditions, and an attestation artifact.
Provide SIEM export contract and example queries so Security Ops can validate completeness and retention in upstream tools.
Specify rollout windows, reviewer assignments, and remediation SLAs for a staged RBAC v2 migration.
Ensure privacy/minimization: evidence contains metadata, not plaintext customer data.
scope: Applies to all RBAC v2 permission grants that confer read/write/export access to customer datasets and any associated service accounts. Excludes internal infra-only roles with zero customer-data affinity (those are handled by infra reviews).
guiding-principles: Evidence-first: every approved grant must be accompanied by machine-verifiable evidence.
Least-privilege by default: reviewers must default to deny when in doubt.
Automate where possible: reduce manual friction for reviewers and auditors.
Separation of duties: certifiers should be different people than approvers that created the grant when practical.
Privacy-preserving telemetry: do not include customer payloads in exported artifacts.
proposed-permission-model: RBAC v2 surface for customer-data access uses a capability-oriented role taxonomy: read-only-data, read-metadata-only, export-ready, data-admin. Each capability is anchored to an enforcement tag (resource classification) and optional temporal binding (time-window TTL). Role bindings must include rationale and scoping attributes (resource patterns, environment, emergency flag).
certification-rubric: Evidence required for each binding: policy snapshot (policy id + version), resolver path (where binding came from), last 90d use summary (count of successful accesses), last access actor and timestamp, associated service principal fingerprints.
Risk scoring: combine sensitivity class (S1..S4), last-use recency, and binding breadth into a numeric score (0-100). Flags above 70 are high-risk and require manager + security review.
Reviewer verdict values: approve, approve-with-conditions (reduce scope or TTL), revoke, defer (needs more evidence).
Condition templates include explicit TTL (hours/days), resource pattern narrowing (e.g., table:customer_2023_*), and monitoring hooks (alert on new principal reuse).
evidence-automation-surface: API: /audit/evidence/v1/collect?binding_id=<id> — returns artifact metadata, signed hash, and reference links (no customer payload).
Batch job: nightly evidence assembler that collates policy snapshots, last-use metrics from tracing, and tokens of attestation from the policy engine.
Console integration: review queue in Console shows evidence artifact link and autogenerated risk score for each candidate.
Export format: JSON Lines (one artifact per binding) with top-level fields: artifact_id, binding_id, policy_version, last_use_summary, sensitivity_tag, signed_by (service account).
Retention: evidence artifacts retained 2 years by default; high-risk artifacts TTL extended to 7 years for auditability.
siem-export-contract: Export channel: compressed daily batches to SIEM via secure push (s3://redwood-siem-ingest/bindings/DATE/).
File format: newline-delimited JSON with schema v1.2 (artifact_id, binding_id, resource_pattern, role, principal, action_set, sensitivity, last_use_count_90d, first_seen, last_seen, signed_hash).
Atomicity: batches must include metadata manifest.json listing file checksums and generation timestamp.
Auth/ACLs: SIEM ingest credentials rotated monthly; pushes must use key-based auth and IP allowlist.
Mapping guidance: SIEM fields should be mapped to: host=resource_pattern, user=principal, action=role+action_set, risk_score=derived_score.
example-siem-queries: KQL: events | where action == 'export' and sensitivity == 'S1' | summarize count() by principal | top 25
Splunk: index=rbac_bindings severity>=WARN | stats latest(last_seen) as lastSeen by binding_id, principal
migration-steps: Inventory: run binding census to identify all roles touching customer-data resources. (JIRA: SECURITY-4412)
Tagging: apply sensitivity tags to resources using classification job; propagate tags into policy engine.
Pilot cohort: select two product teams with varied access patterns for a canary certification cycle.
Automate evidence: enable evidence job for pilot teams and surface in Console review queue.
Reviewer training: 2-hour workshop + checklist document for pilot certifiers.
Broader rollout: expand to remaining teams in 3 waves with 4-week windows, enforced remediation SLAs.
rollout-schedule: Wave 0 (pilot): 2026-02-01 to 2026-03-01 — 2 product teams, security in-path, enable evidence export.
Wave 1: 2026-03-15 to 2026-04-12 — 6 teams (core infra excluded) with automated telemetry enabled.
Wave 2: 2026-04-20 to 2026-06-01 — remaining product and platform teams; enforce TTL on new bindings.
Quarterly recertification: after initial rollout, all bindings related to customer-data will be recertified quarterly.
remediation-playbook: Step 0: Triage — reviewer marks binding with verdict and assigns remediation owner.
Step 1: Immediate mitigation — if high-risk and active access in last 7 days, apply temporary deny-once policy and notify owner.
Step 2: Narrow scope — propose and deploy a scoped binding (pattern narrowing or TTL), re-run evidence collector.
Step 3: Hard revoke — if owner fails to respond within SLA (72 hours for high-risk), escalate to security ops for revocation and incident ticket.
Step 4: Post-mortem — record root cause, identify automation gaps, and add test coverage for future prevention.
acceptance-criteria: Evidence artifacts are produced for >=95% of bindings surfaced to the Console review queue.
SIEM receives daily batches with manifest checksums and no data leakage of customer payloads.
Pilot certifiers can complete a certification cycle in under 20 minutes per binding on average.
Remediation SLA met for high-risk bindings in 95% of cases during pilot.
open-questions: What is the final sensitivity taxonomy (S1..S4) authoritative source? Security classification working group TBD.
Should external vendor service accounts be in-scope for quarterly recertification or on an annual cadence?
How do we handle cross-tenant delegated grants where resource patterns span multiple orgs?
Do we include time-windowed ephemeral grants created via job runners in the same queue or a separate ephemeral review flow?
